articles.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
articles.summary: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

image.caption: The North Korean soldiers, seen here in photos taken at a POW camp in Ukraine last February, had expressed a wish to resettle in South KoreaImage: Kim Hong-Ji/REUTERS

blocks.text: Speaking at the UN General Assembly on September 23, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sparked a diplomatic dust-up with South Korea.

In his speech, Zelenskyy mentioned that Ukraine had recently "sent two North Korean prisoners of war to the Republic of Korea" — men who had been captured by Ukrainian forces during fighting in Russia's Kursk region in January 2025. Both had expressed a wish to resettle in South Korea, he said.

The reaction from Seoul was swift: South Korea's Foreign Ministry summoned Ukraine's ambassador to Seoul, Andrii Vieshkin, and demanded an explanation for what it described as Kyiv's "unilateral disclosure" of the prisoners' transfer, despite a prior agreement to keep the matter confidential, along with an official apology.

blocks.caption: Russia's war in Ukraine has given North Korea the opportunity to strengthen ties with Moscow, in part by sending soldiers to the battlefieldImage: KCNA/KNS/AFP

blocks.text: Responding to Zelenskyy's speech, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war was a sensitive topic with wide-ranging consequences for diplomacy and national security on the Korean Peninsula.
Did Kyiv and Seoul have a secret agreement?

Dmytro Lytvyn, Zelenskyy's spokesperson, wrote on Facebook that no such confidentiality agreement existed between the two countries, adding that it was wrong to keep secret where such prisoners were being transferred.

Soon after, South Korean presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan called Lytvyn's denials false, according to news agency Reuters. Kim said Ukraine had asked for confidentiality — allegedly over concerns there might be criticism at home if the North Korean prisoners weren't swapped for Ukrainian prisoners being held in Russia.
Seoul had agreed to the secrecy for diplomatic reasons, he added, but also to protect the prisoners and their families who were still living in North Korea.
Missed opportunity to 'improve bilateral relations'

Nataliya Butyrska, an Asia-Pacific expert at the New Europe Center in Kyiv, told DW that Ukraine and South Korea lacked a continuous, trust-based dialogue, especially under the current government in Seoul.
"We should actually be natural partners — we should be standing shoulder to shoulder, with North Korea fighting against Ukraine," she said. "But that's not the case, due to a lack of trust."
Why Kyiv and Seoul are clashing over North Korean POWs

The prisoner transfer has been a hotly debated topic in South Korean media in the last week — not least because, according to South Korea's constitution, North Koreans are considered citizens of South Korea. It's also been instrumentalized by opposition lawmakers, while President Lee, aiming to ease tensions with the North, has taken a more measured approach.

"The prisoners could have been used by Ukraine to improve bilateral relations between Kyiv and Seoul," said Butyrska, adding that no one in South Korea was now thinking of thanking Ukraine for transferring the prisoners.

Butyrska pointed out that Russia, which usually doesn't express any interest in foreign prisoners, had actually demanded the return of these two North Koreans. "There was even a period of six months when the Russians refused to release any Ukrainian prisoners of war," she said. "They were not prepared to undertake any swap, because they wanted the North Koreans."
Is Ukraine being held hostage by South Korea's domestic politics?

For some observers, the diplomatic crisis can be linked back to domestic conflicts in South Korea. The opposition wants to know why the president agreed to keep the prisoner transfer secret, and have accused Lee of trying to gain favor with the North.

"President Lee Jae Myung was surprised by the incident, and now wants to shift the blame in part on Ukraine," said Mykola Polishchuk, a Korea expert based in Ukraine. He believes the transfer would have become public knowledge sooner or later, and that Seoul knew that Kyiv was going to comment on it. Reports that Ukraine had asked for secrecy were, he added, a way for a frantic politicians in Seoul to come up with an explanation.
"Ukraine has ended up mired in a scandal which it neither wanted nor planned for," said Polishchuk.
North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine

"South Korea has been pursuing the transfer of the prisoners for a long time. And now everybody seems to be happy that those Korean prisoners are in custody," said Shim Sangmin from the Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul. "But what really complicates the matter is the fact that the South Korean government is trying to make new ways to reconcile with the North Korean regime." He said Seoul was now worried that this transfer of North Korean prisoners could hamper efforts to reestablish communication between the North and the South.

In his view, the Lee government is "more open to the idea of reestablishing ties" with Russia, rather than continuing to cooperate with Ukraine. "That's possibly one of the reasons why this government is skeptical about containing military cooperation with Ukrainian military forces, even though there would be a definite military advantage for South Korean military forces," he added.
Ukraine shouldn't expect military support from South Korea
Butyrska said the latest developments indicate a likely further cooling of ties between Kyiv and Seoul.

"The South Korean government wasn't particularly friendly toward us to begin with, and will now likely keep its distance," she said, adding that it would have been better for Kyiv to have stayed quiet.

In return for a gesture of goodwill and "quiet diplomacy," she added, Ukraine might have seen support from South Korea in another form — technology, for example, especially via third countries. While South Korea isn't directly selling weapons to Ukraine, it does deliver to Poland, Finland, the Czech Republic and Romania, and it's pursuing further integration with the European military equipment supply chain.

For Polishchuk, any cooperation on military technology between Ukraine and South Korea is out of the question, now and in the future. He believes trade and humanitarian help would continue, however. South Korea, he said, is highly unlikely to side with Russia, especially given Seoul's many obligations toward the United States.
This article was originally written in Ukrainian.

articles.title: Turkey's stock market scandal affects nearly half a million investors. Police have made several arrests and an AKP politician has resigned.
articles.summary: Nearly half a million investors are affected, arrests have been made, and a female politician from the ruling party has resigned. What is behind the stock market manipulation scandal in Turkey?

image.caption: Turkey's stock market crisis affects almost half a million Turkish investors and has already caused the resignation of a female politician of the AKPImage: Yasin Aras/Anadolu Agency/picture alliance

blocks.text: Investors in Turkey want one thing above all else: for their money to retain its value. Given inflation of around 30%, that is not exactly easy. As a result, many people are buying gold, foreign currency or stocks and increasingly, mutual fund shares that promise high returns.

But the stock market has become a trap for around half a million Turkish investors. In mid-September, the benchmark BIST 100 index plummeted by 6% in a single day and lost about 12% within just a few trading days.

This sharp drop in stock prices was triggered by a major market manipulation scandal. Approximately 455,000 investors have been affected, more than 45 people have been arrested and a high-ranking politician from the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) has resigned.
What happened?

Everything started when some investment fund providers had trouble making timely repayments to investors. Among those affected were funds managed by the companies Pusula Portfoy and Tera. Two Tera funds alone held assets totaling around €6.5 billion ($6.37 billion).

In response, the Capital Markets Board (SPK) intervened and shut down the funds of seven asset managers, including Tera, Pusula and Atlas. According to the state-run news agency Anadolu, a total of 131 funds are set to be liquidated.

The Istanbul Public Prosecutor's Office is now investigating charges of fraud, violations of the capital markets law and the formation of a criminal organization, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced.
The suspicion: The fund companies are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds, while in reality their funds contained worthless "junk stocks."
Among the 45 people arrested so far are executives from investment firms. In addition, the assets of 42 individuals and 46 legal entities have been frozen, according to Gurlek on X.
The Istanbul Stock Exchange has also taken action: it excluded 27 stocks from the BIST 100 benchmark index as of October 1.
Will investors get their money back?

The funds are being liquidated: Their assets will be sold and the proceeds distributed to investors in proportion to their fund shares. The deadline for this has been extended from three to six months. According to Aysel Gundogdu, an independent financial advisor in Istanbul, this is intended to reduce selling pressure so that stocks are not sold at fire-sale prices. However, this does not mean that the liquidation of each fund will take six months. Depending on market conditions, it may be completed more quickly.

Only, there is no guarantee. An investment fund is not a savings account and any loss in value affects the investor. Gundogdu expects that money market funds will largely be redeemed. With hedge funds and equity funds holding "junk stocks" that are virtually untradeable, however, the situation could prove more difficult.
It is important to distinguish between market losses and damages resulting from potential irregularities.

Economist and columnist Guldem Atabay emphasized that a distinction must be made between price losses and manipulation: Investors bear the market risk, but they do not have to accept false information, artificially inflated prices, or a lack of oversight.
Are the fund company and managers liable for the damages?
If funds are closed or liquidated, the shares and other securities in the portfolio can be sold. The question is how much they are worth and how easily they can be sold.

Financial expert Gundogdu believes that the fund's assets will not cover investors' claims. Furthermore, she says there have been structural failures. "The crisis is far greater than a simple liquidity crisis. There are flaws in management and oversight."
She therefore considers it possible that the assets of the fund founders and managers could also be tapped to make up for the shortfall.

Economist Atabay calls for those responsible to be identified and for the damages to be recovered from them. Following the liquidation of the funds, it must be clarified who is responsible for any legal violations. "Liquidation is no substitute for accountability," Atabay said.

blocks.caption: Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya of the ruling AKP asked Turkish President Erdogan to resignImage: AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What are the political costs of the crisis?

The crisis has already led to the resignation of a high-ranking female politician in the ruling AKP party. Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya, deputy party chair and former minister of family affairs, asked Turkish President and AKP leader Recep Tayyip Erdogan to "relieve her of all her posts." This has been a phrase frequently used within the AKP for years when someone is forced to resign.

She was facing allegations regarding stock transactions by her and her husband, Ilyas Kaya, in connection with the fund crisis. Political responsibility, she wrote on social media, goes beyond legal responsibility. She said her position should not hinder the investigation.

The opposition now intends to bring the issue before Parliament. Selcuk Ozdag, deputy leader of the Yeni Yol parliamentary group, announced that as soon as Parliament reconvenes, he will submit a motion for a parliamentary investigation. The investigation is intended to determine whether politicians are involved in the manipulation scandal.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Trillanes: Firm of VP Sara's husband got P319M from China
articles.summary: Former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV said Friday, October 2, that a food company partly owned by Vice President Sara Duterte's husband took in more than P319 million from China while reporting no…

blocks.text: October 2, 2026 | 12:26pm
Composite image shows Vice President Sara Duterte as seen in June 2026 and her husband, Mans Carpio, in April 2026.
Duterte office; The STAR / Miguel de Guzman; Philstar.com composite

MANILA, Philippines — A food company partly owned by Vice President Sara Duterte's husband, took in more than P319 million from China while reporting no rank-and-file employees, Former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV alleged on Friday, October 2.

Trillanes made the claim at a press conference a day after House prosecutors withdrew their bid to present him as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial. The former senator said he had asked to be dropped to relieve the prosecution of any more pressure and promised to disclose today everything he would have shared during the trial.

The former senator argued the flow of Chinese funds to companies with ties to the vice president had severe national security implications and on its own was enough to impeach and disqualify her from public office.

"Dapat kilabutan po tayo dito... Bawal po iyan. Bawal tumanggap from a foreign government, especially high-ranking official ang vice president," Trillanes said. "Kapag hindi pa ba impeachable iyan, ewan ko nalang. Nagbubulag-bulagan tayo."
Duterte has denied all allegations of possessing unexplained wealth and in April accused Trillanes of repeating the same allegations he has made since 2016, this time with a "machinery backing him."
Cale88's 'red flags'
Trillanes' presentation claims the funds flowed from the Chinese government and Chinese corporations, to Cale88 Foods Corp., a company with ties to Duterte's husband Mans Carpio.

Securities and Exchange Commission Director Gerardo Del Rosario previously testified during the impeachment trial that Carpio was an incorporator, director and shareholder of Cale88 from 2021 to 2024, and that his stake rose to 47.5% in 2024, before disappearing in 2025.

articles.title: Tennessee suspends executions as Christa Pike’s lawyer says failed lethal injection leaves her in critical condition
articles.summary: Independent inquiry ordered after failed execution of Pike, who was convicted of 1994 murder

blocks.text: Tennessee’s governor on Thursday said it was “deeply disturbing” that his state botched the execution of a death row prisoner who remained alive and snoring 40 minutes after receiving a double dose of the lethal drug that should have quickly killed her.

Bill Lee, a Republican, has suspended all executions in the state until at least the end of the year and ordered an independent inquiry after Wednesday night’s failed attempt to put to death Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder, at the execution chamber in Nashville.

Meanwhile, Pike, 50, remained in the hospital on Thursday afternoon. “We don’t have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment, but we do know that she is alive right now and receiving life-saving medical care,” Randy Spivey, one of her attorneys, said at an afternoon press conference.
“She is in critical condition receiving life-saving care. That is the extent of what we have at the moment.”

Spivey, of the office of the post-conviction defender, condemned Tennessee authorities for the manner in which the failed attempt unfolded. He said officials used seven needles, one of which became bent as it was removed from Pike’s arm.

“Last night was not just inefficient, it was cruel and it was torturous. It was also predictable,” he said, adding that he saw no life-saving care given after the execution attempt was abandoned at about 8.25pm.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday morning, Lee said he had spoken with Frank Strada, secretary of the Tennessee department of correction, but did not have an update on the condition of Pike, who was taken to an off-site medical facility after surviving two doses of pentobarbital.

“This is a tragedy,” Lee said, adding that he had not yet spoken to the families of Pike or the teenager she killed in 1995. “There is no one that wanted what happened last night to happen. It shouldn’t have happened.

“It’s the most difficult of circumstances as it relates to the sentence that should have been carried out by the state. It’s a tragedy, and it’s deeply disturbing that that has happened in this state. The people deserve better than that.”
Lee added, in comments reported by the Tennessean, that he had not yet chosen an investigator to lead a “comprehensive, third party review” he announced in a statement late Wednesday.
“There are a lot of questions,” he said. “The people of our state deserve to have those questions answered. I’m highly disappointed, along with Tennesseans, about what happened.”

Cameron Sexton, the Republican speaker of Tennessee’s house of representatives, said on Thursday in a social media post that he and other lawmakers would also be investigating what went wrong with the attempted execution. He added that they would look at other ways to prevent executions from failing.
“We will look at all options – expanding the alternatives, and changing the current medications to include potassium chloride,” he said. “Thirty years is too long for justice.”

Robin Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said her group was aware of seven other people that have survived medical problems due to an execution team’s failure to access a vein to administer lethal injection drugs, but nobody had remained alive after receiving the drugs used in such executions.
“This failed attempt is the worst we’ve ever seen and unlike any other botched execution in the modern era,” she said in a statement.

“What happened to Christa Pike can be attributed to the extreme secrecy Tennessee officials have maintained about their execution procedures, their refusal to answer reasonable questions and their unwillingness to accept responsibility for their mistakes.”
In May, Tennessee officials called off the lethal injection of Tony Carruthers, another convicted murderer, after failing for more than an hour to place an intravenous line into his arm.

On Thursday, Donald Trump was questioned on how an execution like Pike’s could fail, but told reporters they would have to speak to Tennessee officials about that. When someone he was travelling with said “It should be easy to do,” Trump reiterated his words, saying “it shouldn’t be very difficult.”
Pike, who was sentenced to death for the brutal 1994 killing of a teenage classmate, was set to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

The execution attempt was allowed to proceed only after the US supreme court intervened late on Wednesday to lift a federal court stay issued earlier in the day, a delay it said was necessary to assess whether Pike’s allegations of childhood sexual abuse were fully considered at her 1996 sentencing.

Lawyers for Pike filed an emergency motion to the Tennessee supreme court after the second pentobarbital dose was administered asking to halt and stay the execution, saying she was in “unnecessary agony”, and that the state was violating her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment.
A representative of the state corrections department defended its handling of the unsuccessful execution attempt.

“The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the State’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office,” the spokesperson, Dorinda Carter, said in a statement.

“The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility.”

According to the AP, Tennessee’s execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes to be administered “if the inmate is not deceased” after the first set. It does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

Seven journalists who were present at the Riverbend maximum security institution as witnesses described what they saw during a livestream hosted by WVLT television station soon after curtains in the execution chamber were lowered for the final time.
They said Pike was snoring as corrections officials escorted them out.
John North, of ABC News affiliate WBIR, said: “It appears this did not go how this was supposed to go. When we left the building, so far as we knew, she was probably still alive.”

Pike and her boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp were 18 and 17 when they and another female friend tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, one of their classmates at Knoxville Job Corps, in January 1995, using boxcutters and a rock.

The case garnered nationwide headlines due to the ages of those involved and the brutality of the murder, in which Shipp carved a pentagram into their victim’s chest and Pike later showed a friend a fragment of her skull.
Pike never denied the killing, and was later diagnosed with mental health disorders.
“I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” she said in a clemency petition that Lee and the US supreme court denied.

Lee’s suspension order affects the only other execution set in Tennessee this year. Gary Wayne Sutton has been on death row since 1996 for the murder of a friend, and was scheduled to be put to death on 3 December.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: DFA strongly rejects China's claim over Batanes waters
articles.summary: DFA strongly rejects China's claim over Batanes waters

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 12:15pm
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday rejected the Chinese Embassy’s claim of sovereignty and jurisdiction over the waters off Batanes.
“The Department firmly and strongly rejects the Chinese Embassy’s assertion that China has sovereign rights and jurisdiction in the waters off Batanes,” the DFA said in a statement.
This comes after the Philippine Coast Guard recently warded off a Chinese Coast Guard near Cabra Island in Mindoro.

“... The Department affirms that the Philippine Coast Guard was conducting lawful and routine law enforcement operations in response to a suspected unauthorized Marine Scientific Research (MSR) activity in the waters off Batanes,” it added.
DFA said authorities detected the Chinese research and vessel JIA HAI KE 7 approximately 37 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, well within the Philippines’ Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
'No consent'
It emphasized that the Chinese research was conducted without the consent of the Philippines, which is required under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

“Under Article 246 of UNCLOS, marine scientific research in the EEZ and on the continental shelf shall be conducted with the consent of the coastal State. The Philippines did not receive any request from the Chinese side and no consent has been given to any Chinese vessel to conduct MSR,” DFA said.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, the Chinese Embassy responded to a statement by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea rear admiral Jay Tarriela, who called on Ambassador Jing Quan to cease asserting claims over Batanes and urged the public not to give in to harassment.
The Chinese Embassy addressed Tarriela, describing his statement as a “baseless accusation” and “nothing but political theater.”
The embassy said that under international law, including UNCLOS, China holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction in the area due to overlapping maritime claims with the Philippines.

“Under international law, including [UNCLOS], China has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the relevant waters. China and the Philippines have overlapping maritime claims there, and in accordance with international law and the consensus between the two sides, this should be resolved through negotiation,” Deputy Spokesperson of the Chinese Embassy Guo Wei said.

“China firmly opposes the Philippines' illegal actions in waters under China's jurisdiction based on unilateral claims, and will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its own rights and interests,” he added.

In response, the DFA called on China to abide by its international obligations and refrain from counterproductive actions that hinder efforts to restore mutual trust, adding that it will continue to defend the Philippines’ claim in its EEZ.
“The Philippines will continue to uphold the country’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction in its EEZ peacefully and responsibly in accordance with international law,” the DFA said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘No one disrespects Our Lady’: fears for Brazil’s patron saint grip country ahead of election
articles.summary:
Speculation that Flávio Bolsonaro will try to strip Our Lady of Aparecida of position could become deciding factor in run-up to Sunday

A row of Biblical proportions has erupted in the run-up…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: A row of Biblical proportions has erupted in the run-up to Brazil’s presidential election, with the country’s patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida, emerging as an unlikely kingmaker in the deadlocked race.
Ahead of Sunday’s vote, the two frontrunners – the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and his far-right challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro – are level in the polls.

But in recent days, speculation that Bolsonaro – son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro – might strip the widely cherished patroness of her position have caused a nationwide outcry, leaving some to question if it could tip the knife-edge election in favour of Lula, who is Catholic.
“It could sway things one way or the other,” said Thomas Traumann, a political analyst who has been tracking the unusual election row.

It remains unclear precisely how the commotion began, but debate over the issue exploded last week when a remark by Bolsonaro, whose movement includes many evangelical Christians, went viral online. In a recent broadcast, the former senator said one of his first acts as president would be to “decree that Brazil belongs to the Lord Jesus Christ”.

Some Catholics took that as a sign that the Protestant politician planned to unseat Our Lady of Aparecida, although only the Vatican – which declared her Brazil’s patroness in 1930 – has the authority to do so.

blocks.caption: Brazil’s rightwing senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal party during a campaign rally in São Paulo. Photograph: Nelson Almeida/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Those suspicions were reinforced by Bolsonaro’s reported links to JB Carvalho, an evangelical leader who has previously called for the patroness’s removal. In 2007, another Bolsonaro ally tried to introduce legislation to the same effect, although the bill was dropped.

Bolsonaro has called claims he plans to unseat Our Lady of Aparecida “fake news”. He alleged the rumours were being spread by Lula supporters, as well as members of the Episcopal Conference of Brazil, a Catholic bishops’ organisation. The conference rejected the charge.

Lula’s leftwing movement has taken advantage of the furore, keenly aware it could hurt the far-right candidate’s chances in a country where nearly 57% of the population is Catholic. With the result expected to be even tighter than the last one – when Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by less than 2% – even a small number of votes could mean the difference between victory and defeat.

Lula has appeared on the campaign trail holding statuettes of the Virgin Mary while his wife, Janja da Silva, has worn a pendant honouring Our Lady of Aparecida. “As long as I’m president, no one will disrespect Our Lady of Aparecida. No one. People need to learn to respect all religions,” Lula told a rally in the Amazon. Lula’s vice-president and running mate, a devout Catholic called Geraldo Alckmin, published a video describing how he had received messages from Catholics “worried about the direction of the country and the terrible news that has been circulating”. Alckmin assured voters he and Lula would preserve and protect “religious traditions, so sacred to Brazilian families”.
The row speaks to the rivalry and tensions between Brazil’s once dominant Catholic church and the evangelical movement, which has grown rapidly since the 80s.

Traumann said: “It touched a raw nerve, which is the growing power of the evangelicals. Evangelicals make up about 30% of the population, but their political power is much greater than 30% – and within Bolsonarismo it is even more significant”.

Traumann believed that, irrespective of whether Bolsonaro really did intend to remove the patroness, the furore had tapped into “a genuine fear among Catholics of being pushed outside the system”. “I have no doubt that this is going to be important [in the election]. [Flávio Bolsonaro] knows it has landed badly,” he added.

Luiz Antônio Simas, a historian and author of the book So Many Marys: Our Lady in Popular Culture, said the outcry “was a symptom of the popularity that Aparecida and the Virgin Mary in general have in the formation of our culture”.

blocks.caption: Lula at a campaign rally in Belem, Brazil. Photograph: Marx Vasconcelos/Reuters

blocks.text: “For Brazilian popular culture, Our Lady of Aparecida transcends altars … She is extremely powerful as a defining element of what we envision Brazilian popular culture to be,” Simas said, noting how Brazil’s “Black Madonna” was present in samba parades, football culture and Afro-Brazilian faiths.

While the debate flared up on the eve of the election, Simas said Our Lady of Aparecida was a long-running point of tension between Catholics and evangelicals, who oppose the Catholic veneration of saints and images. He recalled a major outcry in 1995 when a neo-Pentecostal pastor kicked a statue of Our Lady of Aparecida on TV.

Simas believed religious racism was at the heart of the outcry, given that Our Lady of Aparecida was a black representation of the Virgin Mary. “When all of this comes into contact with a turbulent political context, in a country experiencing the tensions of a highly contested pre-election scenario, all these controversies come to the surface,” Simas added.

articles.title: US pressures EU allies to release diesel stockpiles
articles.summary: The Trump administration has called on its European allies, particularly Germany and France, to release strategic diesel reserves in an effort to ease fuel prices. The EU will hold an emergency…

image.caption: The Trump administration wants Germany and France to release strategic diesel reserves to stem surging fuel pricesImage: Martin Meissner/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United States on Thursday told its European allies, particularly Germany and France, to "immediately" release their strategic reserves of diesel to help lower the soaring price of the refined fuel.
It comes after President Donald Trump on Wednesday floated the possibility of banning US diesel exports to stem the rise in prices.
Average US diesel prices have surged over 70% to $6.39 per US gallon (€1.50 per liter) since the start of the Iran war, according to AAA motor club data.
The surging cost of fuel has stoked public anger and intensified anxiety within Trump's Republican Party that it could lose control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
Germany's ADAC motoring club on Thursday reported an average diesel price of €2.409 per liter ($10.25 per US gallon).
Donald Trump blames Ukraine for record US diesel prices
What did US officials say?
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News on Thursday that he was "highly confident" Europe could ease fuel prices by drawing down emergency diesel inventories.

"This is a time for a coordinated release of diesel stores as we ⁠go into ​to harvest season and we go into winter heating oil season," Wright told the US broadcaster. "Now's the time to bring ​more diesel to the market, and that diesel is available. I think we have some positive news coming."

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had done its share of an agreement struck in March among International Energy Agency ​members in releasing 172 million barrels of US diesel. "America is doing its part," Bessent said on X. "We look to our allies to match their commitments with action."
"Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions," he added.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, meanwhile, said there was an "eagerness on both sides to work together" on the diesel issue.

"We know that France, Germany, and Italy, ‌they're sitting on reserves ... ‌I won't ​put words in their mouth, of course, but ​I think they would love to have ⁠a ​cooperative path ​forward with the United ​States on how ‌we get more diesel ​to ⁠market," Greer told a news conference ⁠in ​Milwaukee.
How did the EU respond to the US demand?

European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic, who was also attending a two-day G20 trade ministers' gathering in Milwaukee, met with Greer but told reporters that he did not go into details on energy exports.
The EU official said any move by the US to ban diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans."
He added that such a ban would have "very dramatic consequences for our economic performance."
Sefcovic said both sides "decided to stay in close touch to avoid any surprises here."

France's minister delegate for international trade, Nicolas Forissier, told the AFP news agency in Milwaukee: "I can't imagine that there will be a ban." He stressed that both sides will "try to find solutions."
Germany's Economy Ministry, meanwhile, said the International Energy Agency, the West's energy watchdog, has not yet asked Germany to release stocks.
On Friday morning, the EU's energy task force will hold an emergency meeting to discuss the situation, a Commission spokesperson said.
The task force is made up of the European Commission and the 27 EU member ​countries.

articles.title: Ex-Sara aide skips NBI appearance, denies Gracioso cash claims
articles.summary: Jefry Tupas says overseas trips contradict parts of Gracioso's sworn account.

blocks.text: October 2, 2026 | 11:47am

MANILA, Philippines — A former aide of Vice President Sara Duterte did not personally appear before the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) after being subpoenaed over allegations that he received cash on her behalf, but submitted a sworn statement denying the claims.

The NBI had ordered Jefry "Jepoy" Tupas, a former Davao City information officer who later worked at the Office of the Vice President, to appear at 10 a.m. on October 1 as part of its investigation into alleged plunder, graft and money laundering.
Tupas' lawyer Toby Diokno told Philstar.com that his client did not appear in person.
"I submitted his sinumpaang salaysay for him," Diokno said in a message.

Tupas' affidavit addresses allegations by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., who claimed that he delivered suitcases containing large amounts of cash to Duterte and other individuals on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The Philippine National Police has confirmed that Gracioso had been detailed as a member of Velasco's security team, but his cash delivery allegations remain under investigation.
In his affidavit obtained by Philstar.com, Tupas denied Gracioso's allegations and said he wanted to be left out of what he described as politically motivated claims.

"Gaya ng sinabi ko na, isa na akong pribadong tao at wala na akong katungkulan na kahit ano sa gobyerno. Dahil dito, gusto ko na nang tahimik na buhay at sana naman ay hindi na ako idadawit muli sa mga gawa-gawang kwento lalo na sa mga kwento na ang lantarang pakay ay paninirang-puri lamang kalakip ng bangayan sa politika," Tupas said.

("As I have already said, I am now a private citizen and no longer hold any government position. Because of this, I just want a quiet life, and I hope I will no longer be dragged into fabricated stories, especially those whose clear purpose is character assassination tied to political infighting.")
What Gracioso alleged
Gracioso's sworn statement identified a "Jepoy" or "Jepoi," whom Tupas said he believed referred to him, as a trusted aide of Duterte when she was mayor of Davao City.

According to Gracioso, his first encounter with Tupas occurred around 2018, when he fetched Duterte from a private hangar in Pasay and drove her to the Diamond Hotel. Gracioso alleged that Duterte accepted a bag of chocolates but instructed him to hand a suitcase containing P20 million to Tupas.
Gracioso claimed that similar deliveries occurred between 2018 and 2020, with suitcases allegedly containing P10 million to P20 million handed either to Duterte or to Tupas when he accompanied her.

He also alleged that before the 2019 midterm elections, he delivered vehicles to Davao for Duterte, including vans he claimed contained cash and gifts, and was instructed to leave the vehicles with Tupas.

In another account, Gracioso alleged that during an April 2019 trip to Marinduque, Duterte directed him to turn over two large suitcases containing P50 million each, or P100 million in total, to Tupas.
Gracioso further claimed that on September 21, 2019, he delivered two more suitcases containing P50 million each to the Diamond Hotel and that Duterte instructed him to hand them to Tupas.
He also alleged making another cash delivery to Duterte and Tupas in Busay, Cebu, during the summer of 2020.

Gracioso's affidavit cited further alleged deliveries in 2021, including an incident in a house at Valle Verde 2 and another involving more than P200 million allegedly transported in two Toyota Grandia vans to the Diamond Hotel.
Tupas disputes timeline
These allegations were all denied by Tupas.
He said he did not receive money, gifts or vehicles for Duterte. He also sought to rebut several of Gracioso's claims by citing travel records and other documents.

On Gracioso's allegation involving two P50-million suitcases in Marinduque in April 2019, Tupas said he had never been to the province and submitted passport records, airline documents and social media posts that he said showed he was in South Korea at the time. Public reports on his affidavit say he left the Philippines on April 18 and returned on April 22.

Tupas also disputed the alleged September 21, 2019 delivery at the Diamond Hotel, saying he was in Japan during the period cited by Gracioso. He submitted travel records and social media posts in support of his account.

He also rejected Gracioso's account of a cash delivery in Busay, Cebu, during the summer of 2020, pointing to travel restrictions imposed during the COVID-19 lockdown. Tupas cited an executive order issued by then-Davao City Mayor Duterte suspending domestic air travel to and from Davao City beginning in March 2020.
Tupas also questioned the physical plausibility of Gracioso's account that he carried two suitcases allegedly containing P50 million each.

"Ako ay payat at maliit na tao at, dahil nga isa akong 'openly gay person' o halatang bakla, ang kadalasan kong suot na sapatos ay heels. Kaya, sa totoo lang, siguro ay makakadapa-dapa ako kung susubukan kong magbuhat ng dalawang maleta na puno, diumano, ng 50 Million Pesos bawat isa," Tupas said.
("I am thin and small, and as an openly gay person, I often wear heels. So, honestly, I would probably stumble if I tried to carry two suitcases allegedly containing P50 million each.")

Tupas further said he does not personally know Gracioso and denied ever visiting Velasco's residence in Valle Verde. Other accounts of his affidavit, however, differ on whether Tupas said he did not know Gracioso at all or merely did not recall him as part of Duterte's close-in security.
The NBI is continuing to verify Gracioso's allegations and has said it intends to seek the side of other individuals named in his affidavit.

articles.title: New crew makes the quickest US flight to ISS
articles.summary: The SpaceX spacecraft carrying the Crew-13 team docked with the International Space Station in 7 hours and 55 minutes, setting a new record.

image.caption: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in the US state of FloridaImage: Philip Scott Andrews/REUTERS

blocks.text: Four astronauts docked at the International Space Station (ISS) port on Thursday after completing the fastest flight by a US spacecraft to the outpost, NASA officials said.

The SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, with the Crew-13 aboard, lifted off at 11:10 a.m. local time (1510 GMT) from Cape Canaveral, Florida, and within 7 hours and 55 minutes, its capsule, SpaceX Dragon "Grace," docked at the ISS — setting a record for a US trip to the ISS.
The flight by the spacecraft was the quickest so far, not only for Elon Musk's company, but for any American entity, including NASA.
The time taken for a trip to the ISS mainly depends on the distance between the ISS and the spacecraft at the time of launch.
The space station's convenient location allowed the spacecraft to reach it faster.
The last crew, which took off from the United States, took more than 30 hours to reach the station.
A Russian Soyuz spacecraft set the overall record for a flight to the ISS in October 2020, reaching the station in just over three hours.
What do we know about the crew?
The new ISS crew was set to arrive in mid-September, however, its flight was delayed due to a leak aboard the Dragon.
It includes Americans Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Joshua Kutryk, and Russian Sergey Teteryatnikov

Watkins, the Crew-13's commander, became the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit. The crew is slated to stay at the ISS for six months and will be replacing Crew-12, which is set to return to Earth on Monday.

Despite many international cooperation agreements collapsing after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the United States and other ISS partners still work with Russia on the space station.
The ISS has been continuously in use for the last 25 years. NASA has committed to operating it through 2030.
China's new rocket heats up space race, challenging SpaceX

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Fake job posts for delivery company lead to suspicious links
articles.summary: The delivery company has warned against fake hiring posts, saying applications are only processed through its official career pages and recruitment channels

blocks.text: Claim: Delivery company J&T Express is hiring, and interested applicants for the positions of repackers and sorters can apply through the link attached to the job post.

Why we fact-checked this: The posts bearing the claim have been circulating in different Facebook groups, including those named “SSS at GSIS Pension Increase Update and Pension Loan Benefit” and “Wellie Revillame Official Group.” Membership in these groups ranges between 30,300 and 619,000.

The Facebook posts share similar captions and graphics, which claim that the company is hiring repackers and sorters: “Kami ay naghahanap ng bagong kasapi para sa J&T Express. Inaanyayahan po namin ang lahat na interesado. Pwedeng-pwede ang mga PWDs at mga senior citizens.”
(We are looking for new members to join J&T Express. This is open to all interested applicants. [Persons with disabilities] and senior citizens are welcome to apply.)
These job posts claim to offer a salary of P850 per day. Several posts include links to a supposed application form in their captions.
The facts: Both the job posts and attached links are fake.
The official J&T Express Careers page previously warned the public in a September 10 Facebook post about fake hiring notices using the company’s name and branding.
In the same post, the company said that applications are only processed through its official channels, while official recruitment emails should end with @jtexpress.ph.

None of the Facebook accounts and pages used in the fake posts are included on the official website of J&T Express. Legitimate information on employment opportunities can be found on the company’s career page and Facebook recruitment page. These pages show a list of open positions under different departments, their job descriptions, and requirements.
The company has also warned the public that it does not ask for tips or charge any fees at any point during the hiring process.

Fake link, phishing risks: Scanning tool urlscan.io shows that several links in the fake posts redirect users to yet another unofficial hiring platform unrelated to J&T Express in different countries, such as Dubai, Qatar, and Australia.

Meanwhile, results from phishing scanner easydmarc show that some of the links attached to the posts are suspicious. A link from another similar post was also flagged as suspicious by the link checker powerdmac.

A separate analysis using the phishing check tool skysnag returned warning signs with a 51% risk score for all of the links included in the posts’ captions. URL scanner SafeToOpen highlighted that these links are broken, because the links may be offline, blocked, or shown only to certain visitors — a tactic that scam pages use to hide from scanners.
Clicking suspicious links that ask for personal information can expose users to potential scams. (READ: Phishing 101: How to spot and avoid phishing)
Debunked: Rappler has debunked similar fake job opening posts made on various impostor Facebook groups:

items: FACT CHECK: Fake DPWH job ads contain links to shopping sites
FACT CHECK: Facebook post contains fake link for BFP job application
FACT CHECK: ‘BFP job application’ post contains fake links
FACT CHECK: Post on job vacancies not from official DSWD page

blocks.text: – Jade Florido/Rappler.com
Jade Florido is a volunteer for Rappler’s Research and Data unit. She is a third-year Development Studies student at the University of the Philippines – Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Seoul warns 'further action' if Ukraine does not apologise over prisoner-of-war row
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung also accused Kyiv of "attempting to provoke a war on the Korean Peninsula".

blocks.text: South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung has threatened to take unspecified "further action" if Ukraine does not issue a public apology for revealing that two North Korean prisoners of war had been sent to the South.
Ukraine's leader Volodymyr Zelensky made the disclosure to the UN general assembly last week, angering Seoul, who said the move was meant to stay secret.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha on Thursday described the situation as a "diplomatic misunderstanding", adding that Kyiv was "working" to resolve it.
Lee rejected this characterisation on X, saying it concerned "the dignity of the Korean people and the nation".

Lee's office said last week that it was Ukraine that requested for the move to be kept secret, partly to protect the North Koreans' families, and also because Kyiv wanted to avoid criticism that it had given up an opportunity to exchange the soldiers for Ukrainian prisoners of war.
Zelensky's office responded, saying the two countries had no such agreement to keep the move confidential, further escalating the situation.
Lee himself faced heavy criticism at home after Zelensky's disclosure, with the South Korean opposition accusing him of covering up the transfer to appease Pyongyang.
The two soldiers, who were among thousands of North Koreans supporting Russia in the Ukraine war, had earlier told local media they wanted to be sent to South Korea.
Speaking to Ukrainian media on Thursday, Sybiha, the foreign minister, said he "hopes that this situation will be resolved in the very near future".
"We are working on it. For us, South Korea is an important country. And I really hope for momentum, continuation, and concrete results that we are truly achieving with them," he said.
Lee, in response, accused Kyiv of attempting to "bring war on the Korean Peninsula".

"We express serious regret that, instead of acknowledging the facts of the agreement and apologising, they are talking about an imminent military clash between the North and South," he said in an X post.
Seoul has been sympathetic to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion, but has adhered to its longstanding policy of not providing lethal weapons to any country engaged in active war.

articles.title: PDEA warns public vs etomidate-laced vaping products
articles.summary: The Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on Friday warned the public against the misuse of etomidate, a short-acting intravenous anesthetic that has been detected in seized vaping products.

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 10:59am
The Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on Friday warned the public against the misuse of etomidate, a short-acting intravenous anesthetic that has been detected in seized vaping products.
In an advisory, PDEA said etomidate is a legitimate medical drug used in hospitals to induce general anesthesia but warned that using it without medical supervision can pose serious health risks.
These include rapid sedation, hypnosis, loss of consciousness, involuntary muscle movements, and potentially dangerous respiratory and cardiovascular effects.
Aside from illicit vaping products, etomidate has also been detected in other forms such as tablets, powders, and crystals.

"Etomidate is a powerful medical drug, not a recreational substance. Putting it into vape products creates serious and unpredictable risks, particularly for young people who may not know what they are inhaling," said Undersecretary Isagani Nerez, director general of the PDEA.
Illicit etomidate-containing vaping products have reportedly been marketed under street names such as "space oil," "zombie vapes," and "Kpods."
Several territories in the region such as Singapore, Thailand, China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan have implemented control measures in response to the non-medical use of etomidate, PDEA said.
Nerez urged the public not to experiment with or share suspicious vaping products.
"We urge the public: do not experiment, do not share, and do not assume that a product is safe simply because it looks like a regular vape," he said.
PDEA urged anyone who develops unusual or severe symptoms after using an unidentified or suspected drug-containing vaping product to seek immediate medical attention. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: NY's governor appoints special prosecutor in Cornell frat rape investigation
articles.summary: The governor said she'd lost faith in prosecutors overseeing the case and handed it over to New York Attorney General Letitia James.

blocks.text: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed the state's attorney general as a special prosecutor in investigating the alleged gang rape of a woman at Cornell University.

The woman has alleged she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house. The case, which stems back to 2024, was reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight.
"New information has raised serious questions about how this case was handled, and I've lost faith in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee it," Hochul said.
Hochul's announcement removes Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten from overseeing the case.
The BBC has contacted Van Houten's office.
He has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.
Van Houten reopened the case after the civil lawsuit and said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office.
"The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued," Hochul said in a statement.
The attorney general will, if warranted, prosecute any offences found by her investigation and present evidence to a grand jury, the governor said.
James, the state's chief legal officer, said on X that she stood ready "to lead a process guided by the facts and the law".
"The Governor has entrusted my office with this investigation, and we do not take that responsibility lightly," James added.
Hochul and James are scheduled to provide an update on the investigation on Friday morning local time.
The woman at the centre of the case, identified anonymously as Jane Doe in court documents, filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September.
She alleged that she was drugged and raped by seven men at a fraternity house at the university in 2024.
She claimed that Cornell failed to protect her or adequately punish the men, who have now become known as the Cornell Seven.
The case was initially referred to Van Houten, the top prosecutor in the county, in 2024.
Van Houten said his office did not bring charges at the time because he had only seen a statement from Doe implying the incident was consensual and that she had not been drugged.
This week, his office announced it would be reopening the case - less than two weeks after Doe filed her civil lawsuit.

Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.

articles.title: Australia says platforms like Steam and Roblox have 'significant' child safety gaps
articles.summary: Fortnite, Roblox and Minecraft also told to 'lift their game' by online safety regulator.

blocks.text: Australia's online safety regulator has found "significant gaps" in how popular gaming platforms protect children online.

In a new report it found inconsistent approaches in how Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft implement child safety measures as research shows nine out of 10 children aged 8 to 17 in Australia have played online games.

"Australian children have a right to play online without being exposed to predators, sexual extortionists, violent extremist content or other harmful material," eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said.
Weak safety on platforms allow "predatory adults" to make contact with children before grooming them, she said, for sexual exploitation or radicalisation.

The report found that Valve - the US gaming giant that owns Steam and Steam Chat - was the only provider that did not use a type of technology widely used by the industry to detect and remove known harmful content.
Valve also did not "proactively" use tools to detect child sexual exploitation or violent material in chats, with current systems mainly flagging scams, the report found.
Roblox, along with Valve, were noted in the report as using only internal datasets to train language detection systems and for not regularly retraining these models.

"We expect these services to lift their game to identify and combat serious harms such as child sexual exploitation, sexual extortion and material and activity which promotes, incites or instructs violence," Inman-Grant said.

Minecraft and Fortnite, which does offer child accounts, generally let users self-declare their age, the report highlighted, meaning anyone who said they were adults could access "higher-risk communication features".

Steam also relied on users self-declaring their age but the report acknowledged the platform had recently introduced age checks using credit cards, and that Roblox had put in stronger age checks since last December.
Another issue raised by the report was the inconsistent manner in which the four gaming platforms shared information and participated in industry initiatives.
Mojang Studios, developer of Minecraft, and Roblox shared industry expertise in combating child sexual exploitation as well as violent extremism online, but Valve did not.
Elsewhere, Fortnite maker Epic Games failed to share instances of breaches with other platforms under a global programme that was designed to combat online child sexual exploitation and abuse.
The report was based on information collected by Australia's eSafety Commission on how the platforms were protecting users from serious online harm between October 2025 and March 2026.

Australia has made global headlines in recent years for its stance on online safety, after it introduced its world-leading social media ban for under-16s last December - which did not include gaming platforms - and a more recent push to force tech giants to offer users a chance to opt-out of social media algorithms.
Valve, Fortnite, Roblox and Microsoft - which owns Minecraft - have been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Kapunan: Senate should remain ‘safe space’ after Tulfo’s ‘pa-cute’ remark
articles.summary: House prosecutors responded after Raffy Tulfo criticized a lawyer’s conduct during the Sara Duterte trial.

blocks.text: October 2, 2026 | 10:12am
House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan attends the Senate impeachment court proceedings for Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial on Sept. 28, 2026,
Senate of the Philippines via Facebook / Wendell D. Alinea

MANILA, Philippines — House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan reminded the Senate of the Safe Spaces Act after Sen. Raffy Tulfo criticized a lawyer for allegedly being “pa-cute” while questioning a witness in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.
Kapunan said she believed Tulfo’s remark was a misstatement but stressed that the Senate should remain a safe space for women.

“Let me just say that I think the Senate should be reminded that it was the Senate that passed the Safe Space Law. And that Safe Space is the Bawal Bastos Law headed by Senator Risa Hontiveros, also in the House,” Kapunan said during a press briefing on Thursday, October 1.
“So we are believing that could be a misstatement but still believing that the Senate is a safe space for women like us, and for senior citizens like me,” she added.
Republic Act 11313, or the Safe Spaces Act, was signed into law in April 2019 by then-President Rodrigo Duterte.
The law addresses gender-based sexual harassment in streets and public spaces, online platforms, workplaces and educational institutions, among other settings.
In January 2025, the Senate unanimously approved on third reading a bill seeking to strengthen the law.
Tulfo calls out prosecution
During Thursday’s proceedings, Tulfo criticized the prosecution panel over what he said was the presentation of unnecessary witnesses and the conduct of some lawyers.

“Sometimes the prosecution is calling witnesses that are not necessarily needed; we are just wasting our time. You can see some senators get sleepy, some consistently go to the comfort room because it feels useless,” Tulfo said.
“If you are going to get a witness, make sure that they have something to say that can help the ongoing investigation here in the impeachment,” he added.
Tulfo also recalled a recent hearing where a prosecutor was supposedly “trying to be cute” while questioning a police officer.

He advised the prosecution panel to be more mindful of the lawyers it assigns to present witnesses, saying the proceedings should not turn into a combination of courtroom drama and an afternoon variety show.
Tulfo did not identify the prosecutor in his remarks.
What came before
The prosecution has so far presented only one police officer, Police Major Joericson Sangalang of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office.

Sangalang testified on Article II of the impeachment complaint, which involves allegations that Vice President Sara Duterte had unexplained wealth that was not declared in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

San Juan Rep. Ysabel Maria “Bel” Zamora, a member of the House prosecution panel, questioned Sangalang about firearms owned by Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, that were allegedly not declared in Duterte’s previous SALNs.
Zamora later drew criticism online from some Duterte supporters who accused her of “acting cute” while questioning Sangalang.
She responded to her critics by telling them to “get a life” if they could not handle her sass and style.
Tulfo’s comments came amid the prosecution’s presentation of witnesses in the impeachment case.

articles.title: New York's governor removes district attorney from Cornell rape allegations case, appoints special prosecutor
articles.summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor Thursday to oversee an investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house, with the…

image.caption: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., is seen in a photo taken Thursday. (Matt Rourke/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor Thursday to oversee an investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house, with the governor saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney's ability to handle the case.
Gov. Kathy Hochul signs executive order appointing office of N.Y. attorney general as special prosecutor
WARNING: This article may affect those who have experienced​ ​​​sexual violence or know someone affected by it.
Hochul said she had signed an executive order appointing the office of New York Attorney General Letitia James as the special prosecutor.

"Newly released information continues to raise serious questions about the investigation conducted by the Cornell Police Department and the decision by the Tompkins County District Attorney not to prosecute an alleged sexual assault on Cornell University's campus in October 2024," Hochul said in a statement.
"This has, in turn, undercut my faith, and the public's faith, in the District Attorney's ability to effectively investigate and prosecute the case at this time."
Could be taken to grand jury
Hochul said the attorney general would oversee the investigation and, if warranted, present evidence to a grand jury.
"The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued," Hochul said.

items: What to know about Cornell's alleged frat house gang-rape case and the 'Cornell 7'

blocks.text: "This action will ensure that the matter is fully and thoroughly investigated without conflict or bias, and handled independently with the rigor that this matter demands."
A message left for Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten was not immediately returned late Thursday.
Lawsuit filed last month
New information about the alleged 2024 assault, the university's response and the lack of criminal charges at the time has been disclosed over the last week since a lawsuit was filed last month.
The woman, identified only as Jane Doe in court documents, reported the alleged assault to campus police, discussed it with the university's internal investigators and filed a lawsuit in September.

The lawsuit names seven fraternity brothers, the university, the Chi Phi fraternity and others. It alleges that one of the men sent a social media message to more than 50 other fraternity members alerting them to what was happening and inviting people to take part.

Lawyers for two of the men she is suing have denied they participated in a sexual assault. One said his client hadn't touched the woman. Attempts by The Associated Press to reach the other men or their representatives have been unsuccessful.
Local D.A. agreed to reopen investigation
Van Houten, the Tompkins County district attorney, announced earlier this week that he would reopen the investigation after reviewing new information in the woman's civil lawsuit.

He had previously issued a statement defending his initial decision not to issue charges, maintaining that the woman's first account to police did not include allegations that she had been drugged against her will, was incapacitated beyond the ability to consent or was forced into sex.

Under pressure from the public and politicians, including Hochul, the private university agreed Wednesday to bring in outside lawyers to independently investigate how it handled the woman's allegations.

Cornell has said it suspended the Chi Phi fraternity indefinitely and disciplined or expelled some students after Jane Doe reported her alleged assault. The university has declined to provide specifics, citing student privacy rules.

If you’re in immediate danger or fear for your safety or that of others around you, please call 911. For support in your area, you can look for crisis lines and local services via the Ending Sexual Violence Association of Canada database. ​​

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon asked police investigator about murder of Lilie James day before shootings, court hears
articles.summary: Lamarre-Condon asked fellow officer if Paul Thijssen ‘would have gotten away with’ James’s murder if he hadn’t subsequently killed himself

blocks.text: Police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon asked a colleague, a day before he allegedly murdered Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, if a high-profile killer would have “gotten away with it” if he’d not taken his own life, a Sydney court has heard.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

Ben Higginson, who served with the New South Wales police force criminal investigation team in Sydney, told the supreme court trial on Friday about working with Lamarre-Condon the day before Baird and Davies were killed.
The two police officers had been working at a pro-Palestine protest on 18 February 2024 when Lamarre-Condon asked Higginson about work.
Higginson replied that it had been a “bit of a rough time” as he had been investigating the murder of Lilie James.
James, 21, was a water polo coach at St Andrew’s Cathedral school who was killed by Paul Thijssen in October 2023 days after the pair broke up.
CCTV captured Thijssen following James into the school’s gymnasium with a hammer before her body was found. He later killed himself at the Vaucluse cliffs.

blocks.caption: Lilie James was murdered in October 2023. Photograph: Lilie James/Facebook

blocks.text: Higginson became emotional when discussing the case with Lamarre-Condon, noting the crime had occurred at his old school, so it “hit home a bit more”, the court was told on Friday.
But when Lamarre-Condon asked about James’s murder he seemed “blase”, Higginson told the court.
“He thought Paul was stupid for doing it on CCTV,” the police investigator said.
Higginson told the court that Lamarre-Condon then asked if Thijssen hadn’t committed suicide “would he have gotten away with it?”
The investigator said police didn’t only rely on CCTV when examining a crime.

Higginson brought up the 2007 death of Matthew Leveson and told Lamarre-Condon he “could remember the CCTV of [Leveson’s] partner at Bunnings buying tarp, and he ended up burying him in the national park”.
Both police officers then spoke about how cash was more difficult to trace than bank cards and “what avenues detectives look at for suspicious deaths”, the court heard.
When Lamarre-Condon asked about phones, Higginson said he responded: “If you were to leave your phone at home and commit a murder, the phone would be showing up in the vicinity of your residence.”
Higginson said the two weren’t close, but they would chat at work, and he recalled Lamarre-Condon would tell him about his “side-hustles”.
“Apparently he goes to France to buy Hermes bags and resell them here,” he told the court.
The defence lawyer John Stratton SC said during his opening statement that Baird and Davies were fatally shot in “self-defence” after struggles with the policeman.
Lamarre-Condon immediately began cleaning up the scene because he “panicked”, the jury was told.
The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: May heatwaves, deaths, ruined harvests: study of Europe’s summer paints grim picture for the future
articles.summary:
EU Copernicus report shows surface air temperatures from June to August were 2.5C above decadal average

The scorching heat that persistently

blocks.text: The scorching heat that persistently baked western Europe this summer was the worst on record, a report has found, with more than half the continent seared by “very strong” heat stress that felt hotter than 38C.

Surface air temperatures in western Europe from June to August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average, according to an update from the EU’s Copernicus climate monitoring service on Friday, while milder but still deadly heat across the rest of the continent made the summer Europe’s third hottest on record.

The finding comes as a swelling El Niño of unprecedented strength raises global temperatures and supercharges violent weather from South America to Australia. The natural sea warming pattern, which has broken the temperature record months before its expected peak at the end of the year, is expected to cause almost half a million extra heat-related deaths by February.

In Europe, where El Niño’s effects are felt mostly indirectly – for instance, through higher food prices and inflation – the intense heat experienced this summer is the result of fossil fuel pollution clogging the atmosphere.

The report found at least 60% of western Europe suffered through temperatures above 30C on 17 days this summer. In 2003, a year also marked by ferocious heat, this was observed on 11 days, and in 2025 on just seven. The high heat led to a record-breaking 13 days of “very strong” heat stress across western Europe.

Europe saw an abnormally early start to summer-like weather when a powerful heatwave boggled climate scientists in late May, and high heat continued even through September, the report found. Recurring heatwaves, made hotter and more common by climate breakdown, killed tens of thousands of people across the continent while ruining harvests and shutting power plants.

blocks.caption: A cornfield parched by a heatwave in Tarn-et-Garonne, France, in August. Photograph: Huchot-Boissier Patricia/Abaca/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “The consequences extended far beyond temperature records – affecting water availability, energy systems, transport, ecosystems and human health,” said Samantha Burgess, a climate scientist at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. “As the climate continues to warm, events like these underscore the importance of building resilience to increasingly interconnected climate risks.”

Compounding extremes of heat, drought and fire proved particularly damaging. European sea surface temperatures this summer also broke records, the report found, while the continent’s rivers experienced their lowest summer flows in more than 30 years. Hot weather and widespread drought helped wildfires run rampant.

The severity of fire weather conditions in 2026 was the worst that scientists have ever recorded, data published by the European Forest Fire Information System on Wednesday showed. By the end of September, the 680,000 hectares that were burned made it the third-worst on record, behind the million hectares burned by this time of year in 2025 and the 768,000 hectares burned in 2022.
Smoke, one of the greatest environmental threats to human health, spewed 30% more fine particulate matter into the air than the average over the last two decades.

blocks.caption: A firefighter surveys burning trees as a wildfire rages outside, Bordeaux, France, in July. Photograph: Emma Da Silva/AP

blocks.text: “Frankly, after the summer we’ve just had, there’s little new to say,” said Xavier Rodó, who leads the climate and health programme at ISGlobal, a Spanish research institute, who was not involved in the report. “This surge in the number and intensity of extreme weather events is clearly indicative of unprecedented changes in the European climate, as many records have been broken, not only locally, but also regionally and continentally.”

To stave off the heat, doctors and climate scientists have called on governments to stop burning fossil fuels, shade buildings, green cities, and install air conditioning in hospitals, schools and care homes.
